props.title: 28 Days Later
props.initialSlug: Rage virus turns London into zombie apocalypse

sections.content: **28 Days Later** (2002) revolutionized zombie cinema by introducing fast-moving infected and bringing raw digital cinematography to mainstream horror. Director Danny Boyle shot London's empty streets in the early morning hours, creating haunting images that influenced post-apocalyptic films for decades. The film's "rage virus" premise sparked a new wave of scientific zombie explanations, moving away from supernatural origins seen in Romero's **Night of the Living Dead** (1968). The DV camera aesthetic, while initially criticized, established a gritty visual language that later appeared in films like **Cloverfield** (2008) and **World War Z** (2013).

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond horror, impacting how directors approach pandemic narratives. **Children of Men** (2006) borrowed its deserted UK imagery and documentary-style urgency, while **Contagion** (2011) echoed its focus on viral outbreak logistics. The scene where Jim wanders empty London streets became iconic, inspiring similar sequences in **I Am Legend** (2007) and **The Walking Dead** (2010) series.

Boyle's decision to frame the infection as rage rather than traditional zombism opened new thematic possibilities. The film explores how violence and anger spread like viruses through society, an approach later echoed in **World War Z** (2013) and **The Crazies** (2010). The military subplot in the film's third act influenced later works like **Black Summer** (2019) in examining how human survivors often pose greater threats than the infected. movies.title: REC
movies.slug: Spanish found-footage horror about an infection spreading through an apartment building

sections.content: The film's technical innovations changed horror production methods. Its digital video shooting style, necessitated by quick guerrilla filming in London, showed how low-budget aesthetics could enhance horror storytelling. This influenced found footage films like **[REC]** (2007) and created a template for how to make compelling post-apocalyptic visuals on a modest budget. The sequel **28 Weeks Later** (2007) further refined these techniques, while films like **The Last of Us** (2023) series directly reference its visual style.
